standards.name: ISO 9001:2026 Quality management systems - Requirements
standards.edition: Edition 6, published 2026-09 (16 September 2026). Stage 60.60 International Standard published. ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 9001:2015/Amd 1:2024 are shown as Withdrawn
standards.what_it_requires: A documented, audited management system covering how the company plans, designs, buys, builds, checks and improves its products. Certification is optional; customers may ask for it.
standards.why: Battery manufacturers commonly ask suppliers for a certified quality system; starting on the 2026 edition avoids a later transition. Not a legal requirement for sale.
standards.quote: Status : Published. Publication date : 2026-09. Stage : International Standard published [60.60]. Edition : 6 ... Published on 16 September, the 2026 edition focuses on improving clarity ... Certified organizations will have to transition to the new version within the time frame set by their certification cycle. For further information, they should contact their certification body.
standards.notes: iso.org refused the plain fetcher (403); the page was read in a real browser session, where the standard URL redirects to https://www.iso.org/standard/9001. Transition: ISO's own page gives no number of years. A three-year transition (to about September 2029) is stated by certification bodies (for example https://www.pjr.com/iso-standards-and-technical-updates/iso-90012026-whats-changed, read today: 'existing ISO 9001:2015 certifications remain valid for three years') but the accreditation forum's formal transition document was not found today, so the three-year figure is NOT verified from the body that sets it. Price shown: CHF 235.

standards.name: ISO 9001 clause numbers: design and development; control of externally provided processes, products and services; monitoring and measuring resources; control of nonconforming outputs
standards.edition: Numbers below are the well-known ISO 9001:2015 numbers; NOT confirmed against the 2026 text today
standards.what_it_requires: Design must be planned, reviewed, verified and validated with records. Suppliers such as a contract manufacturer must be selected and controlled, measuring equipment must be calibrated and traceable, and faulty product must be identified and kept from unintended use.
standards.why: These four clauses map directly onto an instrument company that outsources manufacturing and sells a measurement product.
clauses: 8.4 (externally provided processes, products and services) - unconfirmed for 2026
standards.notes: The 2026 text could not be opened: ISO's Online Browsing Platform requires accepting terms of use, which I did not do on your behalf. Two secondary pages read today say the 2026 edition 'maintains the familiar 10-section auditable structure and section titles used in ISO 9001:2015' and that 8.2 to 8.7 are substantively unchanged, but neither lists the four clause numbers. The clause numbers themselves were not read on any page today. Confirm against a purchased copy.

standards.name: IEC 61010-1 Safety requirements for electrical equipment for measurement, control, and laboratory use - Part 1: General requirements
standards.edition: Edition 3.0 (2010-06-10) with Amendment 1:2016; consolidated edition 3.1 published 2017-01-10; includes corrigenda (2011, 2013) and 2019 corrigendum to Amendment 1. Stability date 2026
standards.what_it_requires: General safety requirements (shock, fire, mechanical, energy and other hazards) for electrical test and measurement equipment and accessories. Compliance is shown by design review and type testing, normally at a test laboratory.
standards.why: This is the product-safety standard family for a measurement instrument; it is the basis of UL/CSA 61010-1 in North America and EN 61010-1 in the EU.
standards.quote: This consolidated version consists of the third edition (2010) and its amendment 1 (2016).
standards.notes: No published fourth edition was found today. A search snippet from a standards catalogue mentions a draft second amendment (FprA2:2026) in development; not confirmed. How the standard treats stored-energy hazards from a connected battery could not be read (text is paywalled): see not_found.

standards.name: IEC 61010-2-030 Particular requirements for equipment having testing or measuring circuits
standards.edition: Edition 3.0, published 2023-09-20 (replaces the 2017 second edition). Stability date 2026
standards.what_it_requires: Extra safety requirements for instruments whose measuring circuits are connected to devices or circuits outside the instrument. It adds protective means between the measuring circuit and the operator.
standards.why: The instrument's measuring leads connect to customer cells and modules, which is exactly the case this part covers.
standards.quote: IEC 61010-2-030:2023 specifies safety requirements for equipment having testing or measuring circuits
standards.notes: A search snippet mentions a draft European revision (prEN IEC 61010-2-030:2026); not confirmed.

standards.name: UL 61010-1 / CSA C22.2 No. 61010-1 (North American adoption of IEC 61010-1)
standards.edition: Third edition dated 11 May 2012, revised since (search snippets cite revisions of 29 April 2016 and 15 November 2024). Not read on a primary page today
standards.what_it_requires: The US and Canadian version of the instrument safety standard. A recognised test laboratory tests the product to it and authorises its certification mark.
standards.why: It is the standard an NRTL would use to list a measurement instrument for US workplaces.
standards.notes: Edition and revision dates come from search snippets of test-laboratory notices, not from the standards publisher. Confirm the current revision with the chosen laboratory.

standards.name: OSHA Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory (NRTL) programme; 29 CFR 1910.7, 1910.303, Subpart S
standards.edition: Current regulation and OSHA programme pages as read today
standards.what_it_requires: OSHA requires many kinds of electrical equipment used in workplaces to be approved, normally by carrying the mark of a recognised laboratory. The duty sits on the employer using the equipment, not on the manufacturer.
standards.why: A customer who is an employer may refuse unlisted equipment on site, or may need a field evaluation; the CE mark does not count in the US.
standards.quote: OSHA requires NRTL approval for many kinds of electrical equipment when they are used in the workplace ... OSHA's authority is limited to employers ... The CE mark is unrelated to the requirements for product safety in the United States.
standards.notes: Regulation text read at https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/29/1910.303 : 'The conductors and equipment required or permitted by this subpart shall be acceptable only if approved.' Programme page: https://www.osha.gov/nationally-recognized-testing-laboratory-program . 'applies_when: customer pilot' is my judgement: the rule binds the customer, so it can bite as soon as equipment is on their floor.

standards.name: IEC 61326-1 Electrical equipment for measurement, control and laboratory use - EMC requirements - Part 1: General requirements
standards.what_it_requires: Emission limits and immunity tests for measurement, control and laboratory equipment supplied at less than 1000 V AC or 1500 V DC or from the circuit being measured. Compliance is shown by testing at an EMC laboratory.
standards.why: It is the EMC product-family standard for this kind of instrument and the usual route to showing conformity with the EU EMC Directive.
standards.quote: specifies requirements for immunity and emissions ... of less than 1 000 V AC or 1 500 V DC
standards.notes: Page read is the redline version of the same edition. European adoption as EN IEC 61326-1:2021 and a possible fourth edition in development are from search snippets only.

standards.name: FCC 47 CFR Part 15 Subpart B, section 15.103 exempted devices
standards.edition: Current text as shown by Cornell Legal Information Institute today
standards.what_it_requires: Digital devices normally need to meet unintentional-radiator limits, but a digital device used exclusively as industrial, commercial or medical test equipment is exempt from the specific technical standards. It must still not cause harmful interference, and the operator must stop using it if the FCC finds that it does.
standards.why: The instrument is test equipment sold to industry, so the exemption in paragraph (c) plausibly applies; the general no-interference conditions still do.
standards.quote: A digital device used exclusively as industrial, commercial, or medical test equipment.
standards.notes: The section also says manufacturers are encouraged, though not required, to meet the technical standards. Paragraph (j): equipment from entities on the Covered List stays subject to certification. Whether the exemption fits this exact product (for example if it includes a radio module or a general-purpose computer) is a judgement for a compliance engineer.

standards.name: EU Low Voltage Directive 2014/35/EU
standards.what_it_requires: Electrical equipment in the voltage scope must meet safety objectives; the manufacturer does the conformity assessment itself (Module A, no notified body), keeps a technical file and declaration for 10 years and affixes the CE mark. Equipment must carry a type or serial number, the manufacturer's name and address, and instructions in the users' language.
standards.why: Scope is by the equipment's rated voltage: a product rated entirely below 50 V AC and 75 V DC falls outside; a mains-powered instrument (for example 100-240 V AC input) falls inside.
standards.quote: designed for use with a voltage rating of between 50 and 1 000 V for alternating current and between 75 and 1 500 V for direct current
standards.notes: The inside/outside reading for an instrument powered from an external low-voltage supply (so that only the separate power adapter is in scope) is my inference from Article 1, not a quoted ruling; general product safety law would still apply.

standards.name: EU EMC Directive 2014/30/EU
standards.what_it_requires: Apparatus must not emit disturbance that stops other equipment working and must be immune enough to work as intended. The manufacturer can self-assess under Annex II (Module A), keeps documentation 10 years, issues an EU declaration and affixes the CE mark.
standards.why: Applies to any finished electronic apparatus placed on the EU market regardless of voltage. Custom-built evaluation kits for professionals used only at research and development facilities are excluded.
standards.quote: finished appliance or combination thereof made available on the market as a single functional unit
standards.notes: The evaluation-kit exclusion (Article 2(2)) is narrow; whether a pilot unit lent to a customer's production site qualifies is doubtful and is a judgement.

standards.name: EU RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU (consolidated text of 1 January 2025)
standards.what_it_requires: Limits ten substances in homogeneous materials (0.1% for lead, mercury, hexavalent chromium, PBB, PBDE and four phthalates; 0.01% for cadmium). The manufacturer draws up an EU declaration, affixes the CE mark and keeps the file 10 years.
standards.why: Category 9 of Annex I covers monitoring and control instruments including industrial ones. Equipment designed solely for research and development and made available only business-to-business is excluded.
standards.quote: Monitoring and control instruments including industrial monitoring and control instruments
standards.notes: Practical consequence for outsourcing: the contract manufacturer and parts list must be RoHS-compliant from the first build intended for the EU.

standards.name: EU WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU
standards.what_it_requires: Producers register in each Member State where they sell (through an authorised representative if not established there), mark products with the crossed-out wheeled bin, and finance collection and treatment of waste from non-household users for products they place on the market.
standards.why: Monitoring and control instruments are within scope as large or small equipment (Annex III categories 4 and 5).
standards.quote: a legal or natural person established on its territory as the authorised representative
standards.notes: Registration is country by country; only needed once units are sold into a given Member State.

standards.name: UKCA marking (Great Britain)
standards.edition: UK government guidance last updated 21 August 2026
standards.what_it_requires: Products for Great Britain need a conformity mark. The UK continues to recognise the CE marking alongside or in place of UKCA for product regulations where the requirements meet UK needs.
standards.why: A CE-marked instrument can be sold in Great Britain without separate UKCA work, on current guidance.
clauses: The Product Safety and Metrology (Amendment) Regulations 2024
standards.quote: the UK continues to recognise the CE marking, alongside or in place of the UKCA marking
standards.notes: The page gives no end date for CE recognition and does not use the word 'indefinite'. It does not list the regulations covered on that page; check the sector list before relying on it.

standards.name: UN Manual of Tests and Criteria Part III sub-section 38.3 (UN 38.3), via 49 CFR 173.185
standards.edition: 49 CFR 173.185 current text as shown by Cornell Legal Information Institute today (the UN Manual edition itself was not read: unece.org returned 403)
standards.what_it_requires: Each lithium cell or battery offered for transport must be of a type proven to meet the UN 38.3 tests, and a test summary must be available. It is a transport rule for cells and batteries.
standards.why: It does not apply to an instrument that contains no lithium battery. It matters only if the instrument ships with a lithium battery inside (including a backup cell) or if the company ships customers' cells.
standards.quote: Each lithium cell or battery must be of the type proven to meet the criteria in part III, sub-section 38.3
standards.notes: The conclusion 'not applicable to an instrument without a battery' is read from the scope of the section (it regulates cells and batteries and equipment powered by them), not from an explicit sentence. Search snippets say the eighth revised edition of the UN Manual has been in force since November 2023; not confirmed.

standards.name: IEC 62133-2 Safety requirements for portable sealed secondary lithium cells and batteries
standards.edition: Edition 1.0 (2017-02-07) with Amendment 1:2021, consolidated. Stability date 2026
standards.what_it_requires: Requirements and tests for the safe operation of portable sealed secondary lithium cells and batteries under intended use and foreseeable misuse. It is a standard for the cell or battery, not for equipment that tests them.
standards.why: Not a requirement on the instrument. It is relevant only as something customers' cells may be certified to, or if the instrument itself contains a rechargeable lithium battery.
standards.quote: specifies requirements and tests for the safe operation of portable sealed secondary lithium cells
standards.notes: 'Not a requirement on the instrument' is my reading of the scope sentence.

standards.name: ISO/IEC 17025 accredited calibration (and the ILAC mutual recognition arrangement)
standards.what_it_requires: A calibration laboratory accredited to ISO/IEC 17025 has had its competence, traceability and uncertainty statements independently assessed. Accreditation bodies that signed the ILAC arrangement recognise each other's accredited results.
standards.why: A measurement instrument's stated accuracy has to trace to accredited reference standards before a customer will trust pilot data; battery manufacturers' quality systems typically ask for accredited calibration certificates.
standards.quote: The current scope of the ILAC MRA includes the accreditation of calibration laboratories using ISO/IEC 17025
standards.notes: The current edition year of ISO/IEC 17025 was not read on a primary page today. 'applies_when' is judgement.

standards.name: ANSI/NCSL Z540.3 Requirements for the Calibration of Measuring and Test Equipment
standards.edition: 2006, reaffirmed 2013 according to search snippets; reported as placed in withdrawn status by its publisher but still usable in contracts. Not read on a primary page
standards.what_it_requires: A US calibration-system standard best known for limiting the probability of false acceptance in calibration to 2 percent. Calibration providers offer it as a named service level.
standards.why: Some US industrial and defence customers specify Z540.3 calibration in purchase contracts; major providers still list it as an option.
clauses: 5.3 b (2% false-accept limit, as cited by a calibration provider in a search snippet)
standards.notes: ncsli.org returned 403. Read today on providers' pages only that Z540 / Z540.3 is offered as a calibration option (Keysight calibration services page; Chroma service page: 'Three levels of calibration are available: OEM, Z540, and ISO 17025'). Edition, reaffirmation, withdrawal status and the 2% rule are from search snippets.

standards.name: GUM: JCGM 100:2008 Evaluation of measurement data - Guide to the expression of uncertainty in measurement
standards.edition: JCGM 100:2008, with JCGM 100:2008/Amd.1:2026 (nonlinear measurement models) now listed; also JCGM 101:2008, 102:2011, 106:2012, GUM-1:2023, GUM-5:2026, GUM-6:2020 and a compiled GUM suite (2026)
standards.what_it_requires: The internationally agreed method for building an uncertainty budget and stating a measurement result with its uncertainty. Free to download.
standards.why: Any accuracy claim in a datasheet for an impedance instrument should rest on an uncertainty budget built this way; accredited calibration reports use it.
standards.quote: Evaluation of measurement data - Guide to the expression of uncertainty in measurement
standards.notes: The 2026 amendment and GUM-5:2026 are new this year.

standards.name: CE marking steps for this product (summary across BS-09 to BS-12)
standards.edition: As in the directives read today
standards.what_it_requires: Identify the directives that apply, assess conformity (self-assessment under Module A for low voltage and EMC), compile the technical documentation including risk analysis and test reports, sign one EU declaration of conformity covering all applicable acts, and affix the CE mark before placing on the market. Keep the file for 10 years.
standards.why: None of the directives read requires a notified body for this kind of instrument on the self-assessment route.
standards.quote: ensures and declares on his sole responsibility
standards.notes: A non-EU manufacturer selling direct also needs an EU-based economic operator or representative in practice; that requirement was not read today (see not_found).
